blocks.text: Rice is commonly perceived as an expensive staple food in the Philippines. However, market prices often exclude substantial environmental and social externalities generated during production. Building on Teodoro C. Mendoza’s 2021 True Cost Accounting (TCA) study of Philippine rice production, this paper reassesses whether rice remains “expensive” when climate, water, ecosystem and other hidden costs are incorporated into its economic valuation. Using the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s updated Social Cost of Carbon (SCC) estimate of $190 per metric ton of carbon dioxide for 2020 emissions and adjusting it to approximately $239 per metric ton of CO2 in 2026 values, the analysis […]...
